name: Practical Soundproofing for Attached ADUs and Room Additions in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: What are practical ways to improve soundproofing between an attached ADU or room addition and the main house in Los Angeles without overly complicated construction?
mainEntity.text: What are practical ways to improve soundproofing between an attached ADU or room addition and the main house in Los Angeles without overly complicated construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Noise transfer is a common complaint in attached ADUs and room additions. You can significantly improve sound isolation with a few practical construction choices that do not require exotic methods. For shared walls, consider **staggered studs** or even double-stud walls where space allows. This separates the drywall surfaces and reduces vibration transfer. Fill cavities with mineral wool or high-density fiberglass insulation to dampen airborne sound. On ceilings beneath second-story additions, adding insulation and using **resilient channels** or sound-damping drywall can help. Pay close attention to penetrations: recessed lights, duct openings, plumbing chases, and electrical boxes. Seal gaps and avoid back-to-back boxes on opposite sides of the same stud bay. Use **solid-core doors** between units, with quality weatherstripping and thresholds to minimize sound leaks at the bottom. Soft finishes like carpet or area rugs over hardwood can further reduce impact noise in upstairs rooms. Discuss your noise concerns with your contractor and prioritize soundproofing in bedrooms, living rooms, and between kitchens and quiet spaces. These modest upgrades are easiest to install during construction and can greatly improve long-term comfort for both households.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use staggered or double-stud walls where possible, add insulation in shared walls and ceilings, select solid-core doors with good weatherstripping, and seal gaps around penetrations. Resilient channels or sound-damping drywall on critical partitions can noticeably reduce noise transfer.
